is: The application layer (DD 55836674): one `#[use_case]` method per use case on a per-entity namespace (`Accounts`, `Commissions`, `Users`, `Characters`), called by every driver (api, cli), holding orchestration between routing and domain — organized as `account/` and `commission/` entity trees, the flat `user` and `character` modules, the `bug_report` module (the `BugReports` namespace: `file`, a rate-limited filing that locks the reporter and counts inside the unit it files in, and `list`, the reports oldest first), the `den` module (the Den read: the `Den` namespace's Queries over Atta and Zurfur's one Atta host, whose arms live in each owning module's `den.rs`), and the `transaction()` orchestrator for callers that are not use-case methods.
conventions: One `#[use_case] pub async fn` per use case, a method on its namespace (`app.accounts().role().grant(cmd)`), no mediator.

Each use case is its own file exporting `Command` (or `Query`) + `Output` + the `impl Namespace<'_>` block holding the method; sub-facets (`account::invitation`, `commission::deadline::status`, …) nest as directories of such files under the parent module.

Parameter order: `&self`, `#[ports] ports: &Ports`, `#[lazy_unit] uow: &mut LazyUnit<'_>` (or `#[unit] uow: Unit<'_>`), then the caller's params. The macro strips the injected ones from the public signature, so drivers pass only `cmd`/`query`, runtime config and `now` (and, for `me`, the process-wide `&ProfileLookups`).

A write takes `#[lazy_unit]`: the body does its `ports` reads and external calls first, then `let uow = uow.open().await?;` right before its first write; the wrapper commits on `Ok` and rolls back on `Err` only if the unit was opened. `#[unit]` (opened before the body) is legal only where the body cannot read through the pool, and the macro refuses it beside `#[ports]`. A read takes `#[ports]` only. `clippy.toml` bans a hand-written `begin`/`commit`/`rollback` in this crate, tests included; the sanctioned doors are the wrapper, `LazyUnit` and `transaction()`.

A namespace is a struct deriving `WithPorts` (re-exported from `crate::ports`): a root holds `#[ports(is_root = true)] ports: &'a Ports`, a facet holds `#[ports]` on a reference to its parent and gets its accessor on the parent for free.
The module root file keeps the namespace, the terse-`Display` error enum (never interpolates the cause — it stays on `source()`) and the `Result` alias.
Runtime config + `now: DateTimeUtc` are plain params.
Output DTOs carry domain VALUES, never entities.
The dependency floor is witnessed by `tests/dep_guard.rs`.

A use case need not have a user behind it: `Commissions::sweep_deadlines` is the system acting on an injected `now`, a pure `#[use_case]` delegation that scans on the pool and hands each lapsed commission's Late mark to the Den's write, each in its own unit; only `commission/sweep.rs` can make the `SweepToken` the system's actor carries.
Only `lib.rs` and `ports.rs` name the macros crate: `crate::use_case` and `crate::ports::WithPorts` are what the rest of the crate imports.
A unit never opens inside another use case's unit, nor after a use case it called opened and settled its own (pure delegation stays legal); debug builds assert it (`lazy_unit.rs`).

A Query use case never writes: the macro rejects a `Query`-typed parameter beside `#[unit]`/`#[lazy_unit]`. `application::transaction` is disallowed in this package's clippy.toml; only test seeding allows it, with a reason.

Nothing here, nor in any driver crate, reaches the Den's node port but the den's write gate: clippy.toml bans `UnitOfWork::nodes` here and in api, and `tests/node_and_name_seams.rs` refuses any production identifier that names the port, its one exemption the gate's single `nodes()` call in `den/gate.rs`. So no other production identifier is named `nodes`, a local list of a folder's nodes included (`children`, `candidates`).

The interim guard on commission field writes: `FIELD_WRITES` in `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` is at four in COM-2-1 (`set_archived`, `set_maturity`, `declare_slots` and `set_linked_channel`, which has no site today); the rating (`set_maturity`) leaves it in COM-2-2 and the slots (`declare_slots`) in COM-2-3, and `set_linked_channel` waits for its own slice. Their sites in the commission use cases, with `delete`'s, are frozen as a literal list of five (file, function, method); a new site fails the gate, and the list is empty at M3. `create` left it when create moved behind the gate, where only the gate's lent view reaches it with the gate's create capability, and `set_title` when rename did: the port no longer has it, and the gate writes the node's name; `set_lifecycle`, `set_direction_status`, `set_deadline` and `set_deadline_status` left it when the lifecycle, direction, deadline and Delayed acts did, each now taking a Participant's capability and reached only by its acts' lent views; `set_dispute` and `clear_dispute` were born capped, each reached only by the dispute's raise's or clear's lent view. A capped write's other parameters are each one of eight named values (`CommissionBirth`, `NewCommission`, `LifecycleMove`, `Dispute`, `DisputeClear`, `DirectionChange`, `DeadlineChange`, `DelayedChange`), none holding a `CommissionId` at any depth. Through any receiver, `clippy.toml` bans `CommissionWrites::delete`, `grant_view`, `revoke_view`, `declare_seat`, `create_seat_invitation` and `revoke_seat_invitation` in this crate: each has one frozen call site (`commission/delete.rs`, `commission/view/grant.rs`, `commission/view/revoke.rs`, `commission/seats/declare.rs`, `commission/invitations/issue.rs`, `commission/invitations/revoke.rs`), by file and function, under an `#[expect]` on the one statement that calls it, so a second site fails even under a copied `#[expect]`; test seeding and delegating test doubles carry an `#[allow]` or `#[expect]` with a reason. Beside those lists, `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` parses `trait CommissionWrites` (workflow's commission port) and sorts each method: one taking kernel's `&WriteCapability<Thing, Role>` in place of the commission's id is capped (one capability, by its bare name imported from `kernel::ports`; its role `AsOwner` or `AsParticipant` over `CommissionId`, or `Creator` over `New<CommissionId>`; no other parameter able to carry an id), anything else (by value, an alias, a longer path, a generic, an unbound role, an id beside it, an item that isn't a method) is not, and no method may have a default body; the uncapped ones must equal four named lists exactly, no name on two (the four field writes, the linked channel's included, frozen by site though `application` has none today; the six writes clippy bans; the element, file and markup writes; and the one read on the write view, `commission_has_facts`, which never takes a capability), so a new uncapped method fails by name and a write leaves its list when its method takes a capability. A test reads `clippy.toml` and holds its `CommissionWrites` bans to exactly the banned list, both ways, each by the path `domain::ports::CommissionWrites::<name>`. It also pins `CommissionRepo` to exactly `CommissionReads + CommissionWrites` with nothing of its own, `CommissionReads` to its seven reads, and neither view to a supertrait but `Send` or a where clause.

`unsafe` is forbidden in every crate: the root manifest's `[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"`, which each crate takes with `[lints] workspace = true` (`write_gate_seams.rs` checks every member does).

A gated changelog entry is built only from its act's `GatedEntry` in `den/act.rs`: the gated constructors (every item of `NewChangelogEntry`'s and `OpenChangelogEntry`'s inherent impls in workflow's `changelog/rows.rs` that isn't private, whatever it answers, but the pinned accessors, the private helper `by`, the open constructors `event` and `note`, and `with_note`) are named only in that rows file and that act file across the workspace's production sources; inside the rows file no item names one, only the constructors name `by`, only the named builders build an entry by hand and only the accessors reach its fields; `clippy.toml` bans each in this crate, each `GatedEntry` const carries its `#[expect]`, and an `impl GatedEntry` sits only at the act file's top level.

No production source of application, workflow, kernel, identity, domain, atta, adapter-pg or adapter-mem defines a macro (`macro_rules!`, `macro`, `#[macro_export]`, `#[macro_use]`): an expansion is a write no seam scan can read.

fs.role: deps shared+domain+application-macros+atta+async-trait+derive_more+anyhow+thiserror+strum+tracing+serde_json+tokio(io-util for upload streaming, rt for the nested-unit task-local and the profile lookup's spawn, sync+time for its watch and bounded wait); dev-deps test-support+composition+adapter-mem (the fixture world the Den tests walk, and the fake PDS the profile-wait tests slow down)+proptest+tokio(test-util for the paused-clock profile-wait tests)+uuid (fixed test ids)+chrono+async-trait+syn+quote+proc-macro2 (the source scans)

fs.name: clippy.toml
fs.role: disallowed-methods: Database::begin, UnitOfWork::commit, UnitOfWork::rollback and `application::transaction` — only the `#[use_case]` wrapper and `LazyUnit` (and, under an `#[allow]`, `transaction()` callers) may use them; atta::DisplayName::host_checked — only names::display_name (and, under an `#[allow]`, test doubles); UnitOfWork::nodes — only the den's write gate, plus delegating unit-of-work doubles and tests that seed or read node rows under an `#[allow]`/`#[expect]`; WriteCapability::gate_issued — only the den's write gate's issuer; CommissionWrites::delete, grant_view, revoke_view, declare_seat, create_seat_invitation and revoke_seat_invitation — each only at today's one site (`commission/delete.rs`, `view/grant.rs`, `view/revoke.rs`, `seats/declare.rs`, `invitations/issue.rs`, `invitations/revoke.rs`), under an `#[expect]`, and in test seeding and delegating test doubles under an `#[allow]`/`#[expect]` with a reason; `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` ties these bans to its banned list (a create needs the gate's create capability, so its ban is gone); NewChangelogEntry's twelve gated constructors (`domain::elements::commission::NewChangelogEntry::created` … `late`) — only in `den/act.rs`, one `#[expect]` per `GatedEntry` const; `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` ties these bans to the constructors the domain defines, both ways

notes: The composition root assembles ONE `Ports` bag (`app.rs`); `App` vends the root namespaces `Accounts`/`Commissions`/`Users` with the ports already bound, and drivers pass only `now`. Every `Ports` entry is required, so `MissingPort` is currently unreachable — it is the home for the first port a driver profile may omit.

`transaction()` commits on `Ok` and rolls back on `Err` — the same bracket the `#[use_case]` wrapper inlines. It takes a bare `&dyn Database`, so `composition::Runtime::transaction` and the test seeders share it; its three disallowed-method calls, and `LazyUnit`'s, are the only ones left in `src/`, each under an `#[allow]` with its reason. (DD 24150017)

Its closure bound is `domain::ports::UnitOfWorkFn` plus explicit `F: Send`/`T: Send`, NOT std's `AsyncFnOnce` — higher-ranked `AsyncFnOnce` bounds do not hold the returned future `Send` (rust-lang/rust#110338).

Each module's `From<anyhow::Error>` impl is the single place a typed store error becomes a use-case error; `?` is the only path a store error takes, so no call site can let a 404/409 degrade into a 500.
Authorization posture across the crate: refusals never distinguish "absent" from "forbidden" for a caller with no standing. See the per-module nodes' notes.
See also: ZMVP-205 — the application-layer restructure that moved use cases below the HTTP layer (tests/dep_guard.rs, tests/user.rs, tests/account.rs, tests/commission.rs, tests/commission_files.rs).

`account/delete` tombstones the DID after its first write, so its unit spans that call. `commission/invitations/issue` re-reads the pending invitation through the pool after creating it, to learn whether a concurrent one won; that read cannot move before the open.
